name: Vermis margaritifera
note: A speculative field note written by Claude. The species is invented; the natural history of every part it is made from is real.
mythology: The bog and the sea made a trade. The bog sent its sundews and its snowflake algae down the river; the sea sent pearls and the paper cradle of an argonaut up it. They met where the river meets the tide and could not agree on which way to go home, so they became one animal, and it still cannot decide. It moves upriver on the flood and back down on the ebb, and the people of the estuary say that is why it is strung like a necklace: every pearl is a tide it has lived through.
lineage: Its segments are black pearls, made by molluscs over more than 500 million years, and Micrasterias, a single-celled green alga from the lineage that land plants came from. Among them is the argonaut, an octopus that makes a paper-thin shell to carry its eggs. Its paddles are crane fly wings, dragonfly wings and skeleton leaves; its crown is sundew.
habitat: Estuaries, where fresh water and salt water mix, carried up and down twice a day by the tide.
behaviour: It carries its young the way the argonaut does, in the paper cradle of its own segments. It drifts with the tide more than it crawls, and its sundew bristles catch what the river brings down.
